facts.fact: Corporal Kandan and nine volunteers (Vasu, Sankaran, Kuttan and six others) defy Muthu's order and come down from the wall to hold the cart road at the lightning boulder.

Devan sends the leopard (Neela) up the lip alone to look before Koman speaks; after Koman locates the mirror man, the rest of the Company goes up on Devan's word, 'Left of the cut. Alive, if you can.'

Koman, the old guild watcher from the village above the gorge, is hired on Devan's personal word at seven panam to the moon, paid from Devan's pocket. He reads twenty-three raiders and one man with brass on the lip.
The raiders' bronze signal mirror has a folded-wing sunbird scratched beside the handle (clue C10). Devan does not understand it.
At first light a glint flickers on the lip and Devan's count of six hundred runs out before the mirror is taken; it flashes only briefly and no answer is known.

The captured sergeant says the advance guard carries cutting-saws, mortar lime and seed barley, with orders to hold the pepper hills through the dry season and leave vines and cooperative villages standing, and that the admiral expects the queen not to come.
Vellan will not yet say Asha's last words: 'When I've earned saying it.'
Neela returns Kandan's gourd and says his name aloud; he answers 'Neela'.
